Verdict: Not ready for registration. The 37-row modern-era universe is complete against the cited Wikipedia table, but the single-source grounding claim does not hold for multiple derived `Cause Category`, `Specific Trigger`, and one `Affected Region` value, and one staged `Year` conflicts with the source Date-column rule. These are repairable, but they affect answer-key cells.

Findings:
1. Several derived value cells are not grounded by the cited master table's Notes/Country columns.
   - Type/severity: factual, BLOCKING.
   - Evidence from staged artifacts: `draft.json::temporal_note`, `_extraction_notes`, and `curation.json::source_coverage_notes` repeatedly claim that `Cause Category` is derived from the source Notes column and `Specific Trigger` is a 1-line paraphrase of that Notes column; `Affected Region` is said to come from the source Country column, with only four documented NaN resolutions.
   - Evidence from cited ground-truth source: the master table is headed `Name / Date / Country / Notes / Ref` (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_stock_market_crashes_and_bear_markets`, line 113). Multiple staged derived cells use details not present in that row's Notes/Country cells:
     - `Recession of 1937-1938`: staged trigger says Federal Reserve tightening and fiscal contraction; source Notes say the fall was triggered by a recession within the Great Depression and doubts about the New Deal, not Fed/fiscal tightening (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_stock_market_crashes_and_bear_markets`, line 140).
     - `Kennedy Slide of 1962`: staged category/trigger says `Speculative bubble` and overvalued bull-market/JFK steel-price intervention; source Notes only say it is also known as the Flash Crash of 1962 (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_stock_market_crashes_and_bear_markets`, line 141).
     - `1980s oil glut`: staged Affected Region is `Worldwide` and trigger says oil prices collapsed after OPEC overproduction; the source row has Date `1981-1986`, Country/linked entity `OPEC`, and no explanatory Notes text beyond a reference marker (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_stock_market_crashes_and_bear_markets`, line 146). This is not one of the four documented NaN Country resolutions.
     - `Souk Al-Manakh stock market crash`: staged trigger says collapse of an unregulated Kuwaiti informal stock exchange; source row gives the name/date/country but no Notes text supporting the trigger wording (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_stock_market_crashes_and_bear_markets`, line 147).
     - `1999 Greek stock market crash`: staged trigger says burst of an Athens Stock Exchange speculative run; source row has country Greece and a reference marker, but no Notes text grounding that trigger (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_stock_market_crashes_and_bear_markets`, line 165).
     - `2010 flash crash`: staged category/trigger says algorithmic trading failure; source Notes only say the Dow suffered a near-1000-point intraday drop before partially recovering (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_stock_market_crashes_and_bear_markets`, line 182).
     - `August 2011 stock markets fall`: staged category/trigger says sovereign debt crisis and S&P downgrade from AAA to AA+; source Notes describe a short-lived S&P 500 bear market and decline/rebound, without the downgrade language in the Notes cell (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_stock_market_crashes_and_bear_markets`, line 183). The reference titles later mention downgrade, but the artifact contract says the staged cause/trigger comes from the Notes column.
     - `2022 stock market decline`: staged trigger says persistent inflation, Fed rate hikes, and Russia-Ukraine war; source Notes only report index declines through 2022 (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_stock_market_crashes_and_bear_markets`, line 189).
   - Impact: this is blocking because `Cause Category` and `Specific Trigger` are the causal core of the instance. A reader could not reconstruct these answer-key values from the declared single source and the documented Notes-column derivation rule. Minimal repair: either (a) add per-event Wikipedia articles or other cited sources for rows whose cause/trigger details are not in the master Notes column, updating `source_count`, `source_urls`, and source-role prose; or (b) simplify/rewrite unsupported cells to only what the master table actually says, possibly marking sparse-note rows as less specific.

2. `Bear Market of 1970` has a Year value inconsistent with the cited Date column and the documented Year rule.
   - Type/severity: factual, BLOCKING.
   - Evidence from staged artifacts: CSV stages `Bear Market of 1970,1970,...`. `draft.json::temporal_note` says Year is the 4-digit start year extracted from the source Date column; `curation.json::normalization_decisions` says the Year filter is mechanical and takes the first 4-digit year from the Date column. `_extraction_notes` also lists the cause distribution as including `1968`, which conflicts with the CSV's `1970` value.
   - Evidence from cited ground-truth source: the master table row for `Bear Market of 1970` has Date `Nov 1968`, not 1970 (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_stock_market_crashes_and_bear_markets`, line 142).
   - Impact: blocking because `Year` is an exact-match numeric answer-key column. Minimal repair: either change the CSV Year to `1968` and update table-title/narrative if needed, or explicitly redefine `Year` as a canonical event-name/year convention rather than source Date-column extraction. If the latter path is chosen, the artifact must also reconcile the 2008 exception and the extraction notes so the rule is not internally contradictory.

3. The table-title scope is broader than the cited source title.
   - Type/severity: scope-related, NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE.
   - Evidence from staged artifacts: `table_title` asks for `modern financial crises and stock market crashes`. The cited source is specifically `List of stock market crashes and bear markets`, and the article itself states that it is a list of stock market crashes and bear markets (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_stock_market_crashes_and_bear_markets`, lines 108-110). The same Wikipedia page's See also section links separate broader pages such as `List of banking crises` and `List of economic crises` (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_stock_market_crashes_and_bear_markets`, lines 204-207).
   - Impact: not blocking if the curator keeps the source-defined scope, because `collection_summary` and `source_coverage_notes` disclose the source. But for registration, the title should be tightened to something like `modern stock market crashes and bear markets from 1929 through 2025` or `modern entries in Wikipedia's List of stock market crashes and bear markets` so it does not imply an exhaustive list of all modern financial crises.

4. Sort-order documentation is stale.
   - Type/severity: structural, NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE.
   - Evidence from staged artifacts: `curation.json::normalization_decisions` says the CSV is sorted alphabetically by Crisis name. Local inspection shows the CSV is in chronological/source-table order from `Wall Street crash of 1929` through `2025 stock market crash`, not alphabetical. For example, alphabetic order would place `1973-1974 stock market crash` before `Wall Street crash of 1929`.
   - Evidence from cited ground-truth source: the source table is chronological, beginning with 1637 and then continuing through the modern rows from 1929 to 2025 (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_stock_market_crashes_and_bear_markets`, lines 113-139 and 193-199).
   - Impact: non-blocking because the CSV order does not affect PK uniqueness or row correctness. Minimal repair: change the sort-order note to say the CSV follows source chronological order, or actually sort alphabetically and update any temporal-axis caveats.

Pass checks and spot checks:
- Universe completeness: PASS. The cited table has 23 pre-1929 entries from Tulip mania through Panic of 1907 (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_stock_market_crashes_and_bear_markets`, lines 114-138), then 37 modern entries from Wall Street crash of 1929 through 2025 stock market crash (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_stock_market_crashes_and_bear_markets`, lines 139-199). Local name comparison found no missing or extra staged rows after normalizing dash variants.
- Year boundary: PASS for inclusion/exclusion. 1929 Wall Street Crash is included and source line 139 is the first modern row under the staged filter; pre-1929 rows are excluded.
- Cause/trigger spot-checks with adequate source support: PASS for several canonical rows. 1929 margin/leverage + bubble wording is grounded by the source's description of a speculative bubble and loans being called (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_stock_market_crashes_and_bear_markets`, line 139). 1990 External shock is grounded by the Iraq/Kuwait oil-price note (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_stock_market_crashes_and_bear_markets`, line 154). 2008 Real estate bubble / subprime trigger is grounded by growing housing bubble, subprime loans, credit-default swaps, and bank-failure language (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_stock_market_crashes_and_bear_markets`, lines 170-178). 2020 COVID external shock is grounded by the COVID-lockdowns recession note (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_stock_market_crashes_and_bear_markets`, line 188). 2024 Tokyo currency/yencarry wording is grounded by the yen/rate/carry-trade note (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_stock_market_crashes_and_bear_markets`, line 192). 2025 tariff trigger is grounded by the tariff and retaliation note (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_stock_market_crashes_and_bear_markets`, lines 193-199).
- 2008 Year normalization: conditionally PASS. Although the Date cell includes `11 Oct 2007` and `16 Sep 2008`, the source row name is `2008 financial crisis`, the notes emphasize acceleration on September 16, 2008, and the curation file explicitly documents the canonical 2008 convention. This is defensible if the Year rule is rewritten as a convention with exceptions rather than pure first-year extraction.
- Four documented NaN Country resolutions: mixed but not independently blocking beyond Finding 1. `October 27, 1997, mini-crash` -> `Worldwide` is directly supported by `Global stock market crash` (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_stock_market_crashes_and_bear_markets`, line 163). `Economic effects of the September 11 attacks` -> `United States` is defensible from the event target but the Notes emphasize global stock-market effects (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_stock_market_crashes_and_bear_markets`, line 167). `Stock market downturn of 2002` -> `United States` is plausible but the Notes explicitly list United States, Canada, Asia, and Europe (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_stock_market_crashes_and_bear_markets`, line 168). `2018 cryptocurrency crash` -> `Worldwide` is plausible for a global asset class but the source Notes enumerate S&P 500, Bitcoin, DJIA, and Shanghai Composite rather than saying `Worldwide` (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_stock_market_crashes_and_bear_markets`, line 187). If the curator repairs Finding 1 by adding per-event/value sources, these should be revisited.
- Category/operation/domain: PASS. `query_category=causal`, `secondary_category=temporal`, and `operation_type=projection` fit a table with cause-attribution columns. `domain=Business/Economics` matches the taxonomy's Business/Economics label for markets/finance/economics.
- Preflight: PASS except for the content blockers above. CSV has 37 rows x 5 columns; header matches `draft.json::columns`; `Crisis` PK is unique; no blank cells; `source_count = 1 = len(source_urls)` mechanically; row count is >= 10; `claim_type=source_defined` is recorded.

Final counts:
- Severity: BLOCKING 2 / NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE 2 / SUGGESTION 0.
- Issue type counts: factual 2 / structural 1 / scope-related 1.
- Ready / Not ready: Not ready.

Minimal fixes needed:
1. Add per-event/value sources for rows where the master Notes column is too sparse for the staged Cause Category / Specific Trigger, or rewrite those derived cells to match the master Notes column only.
2. Repair `Bear Market of 1970` Year under a consistent Year convention: either source-Date `1968` or a documented canonical-name-year rule.
3. Tighten `table_title` / source-scope wording to `stock market crashes and bear markets` unless the universe is broadened with additional sources.
4. Fix the sort-order note to chronological/source order or sort the CSV alphabetically.

But multiple retained answer-key cells still require external knowledge or linked-article details beyond that Notes column.
   - Evidence from cited ground-truth source:
     - `Recession of 1937-1938`: staged trigger is `Federal Reserve tightening and fiscal contraction during Great Depression`; source Notes say the fall was triggered by a recession within the Great Depression and doubts about New Deal effectiveness, not Fed tightening/fiscal contraction (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_stock_market_crashes_and_bear_markets`, line 140).
     - `Early 1980s recession`: staged trigger says `Volcker Federal Reserve rate hikes`; source Notes say only rising interest rates to tame double-digit inflation caused the decline, without naming Volcker or the Federal Reserve (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_stock_market_crashes_and_bear_markets`, line 145).
     - `Black Monday`: staged trigger says `Program trading and portfolio insurance feedback loops`; source Notes support program trading and illiquidity, but not portfolio insurance (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_stock_market_crashes_and_bear_markets`, line 149).
     - `1997 Asian financial crisis`: staged trigger says Thai baht devaluation; source Notes describe investors deserting emerging Asian shares, overheated Hong Kong market, and crashes across Thailand/Indonesia/South Korea/Philippines, but do not mention baht devaluation (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_stock_market_crashes_and_bear_markets`, lines 158-162).
     - `Stock market downturn of 2002`: staged trigger says continuation of dot-com bust amid Enron/WorldCom accounting scandals; source Notes describe a 2002 stock-price downturn across the United States, Canada, Asia, and Europe after post-9/11 recovery, but do not mention dot-com continuation or Enron/WorldCom (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_stock_market_crashes_and_bear_markets`, line 168).
     - `2015-16 Chinese stock market crash`: staged trigger says collapse after a government-promoted stock rally; source Notes say the Chinese stock market crashed in June, kept falling, and had a January 2016 sell-off that set off a global rout, but do not mention a government-promoted rally (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_stock_market_crashes_and_bear_markets`, line 184).
     - `2022 Russian stock market crash`: staged trigger says Western sanctions following the Russian invasion of Ukraine; source Notes say the MOEX fell in reaction to the upcoming invasion, then markets were closed by Russia's central bank and later reopened still down, but do not mention Western sanctions as the cause (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_stock_market_crashes_and_bear_markets`, line 190).
   - Impact: blocking because `Cause Category` and `Specific Trigger` are answer-key cells and the instance is explicitly single-source. Minimal repair: either rewrite retained triggers/categories to only use the master Notes wording, or add per-event/value sources and update `source_count`, `source_urls`, and source-role prose. A conservative single-source repair would also reconsider whether rows like 1937, 2002, 2015-16 Chinese, and 2022 Russian satisfy the new `Notes documents a clear proximate cause` filter if the desired staged cause is not actually in the Notes text.

   - Type/severity: scope-related, NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE.
   - Evidence from staged artifacts: `draft.json::temporal_note` and the updated pipeline section of `_extraction_notes` correctly say the universe is 30 rows after `Year >= 1929` plus `Notes column documents a clear cause`. However, `curation.json::collection_summary` still says the instance lists 37 modern financial crises/stock market crashes and that the 37-row universe is just the `Year >= 1929` subset. `curation.json::source_coverage_notes` still says the 37 staged rows are filtered via `Year >= 1929` and that any of the 37 events can be spot-checked. The dropped sparse-note rows are correctly described as sparse by the source: Kennedy Slide has only an alias note (`line 141`); 1980s oil glut and Souk Al-Manakh have no cause note in the visible table (`lines 146-147`); 1999 Greek has no cause note (`line 165`); 2010 flash crash, August 2011 fall, and 2022 stock market decline describe magnitude/effects without a cause (`lines 182-183 and 189`).
   - Impact: non-blocking because the CSV, title, and `temporal_note` reflect the repaired universe, and the post-audit paragraph documents the repair. It should still be cleaned because registration readers will see contradictory universe counts and stale dropped-row examples.

3. Chronological tie-order claim is slightly overstated.
   - Type/severity: structural, NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE.
   - Evidence from staged artifacts: `normalization_decisions` says the CSV is sorted chronologically by Year, then by Crisis name within a year. Local preflight confirms Year is ascending, but the 1989 tie is in source order rather than Crisis-name order: `Rio de Janeiro Stock Exchange Crash` appears before `Friday the 13th mini-crash`, while name-within-year sorting would put `Friday...` before `Rio...`.

So the data order is defensible as source chronological order; only the tie-breaker prose is inaccurate.
   - Impact: non-blocking. Minimal repair: change the sort note to `source chronological order / Year ascending, preserving source order within tied years`, or reorder the tied 1989 rows if the curator really wants Year+name sorting.
